subject: Decision: Antheum Dedicated port — sizing confirmation & cutover cadence
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@antheum.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Antheum traffic profile + ask: sizing confirmation for Dedicated port

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

Thanks again for the deep dive earlier this week. We ran an export of a representative week (attached) and wanted to confirm the sizing assumptions ahead of our commercial signature. High level: hosted API today (multi-tenant) — ~1.1M tokens/day average, 95th p95 requests ~420 reqs/sec globally, with pronounced evening peaks in US-West. Our SLA target for the dedicated migration will be 99.9% availability and p99 latency under 550ms for interactive completion requests.

Quick asks: 
- Can Redwood confirm an initial GPU sizing recommendation (count + instance class + preferred quant profile) that meets p99 latency target while keeping steady-state cost within the committed monthly budget?
- We’d prefer a staged cutover with a canary (5% traffic) for 48–72h, then a linear ramp to 100% over 6–8 hours. Any operational constraints to that cadence?
- Do you need additional traffic slices or longer tail samples to validate KV-warmup behavior?

Attachments: antheum-7day-traffic-sample.csv, SLA_requirements_Antheum.pdf

Goal: finalize sizing & mutually agreed cutover week for the contract signature next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform — Antheum
elaine@antheum.com

---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@antheum.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Antheum traffic profile + ask: sizing confirmation for Dedicated port

Elaine — thanks for the sample and SLA doc. I reviewed the CSV quickly and pasted a very rough starter estimate into the attached workbook (prelim-sizing-estimate-antheum.xlsx). High level thoughts up front: 

- Preliminary sizing: 4 x L4-like GPU nodes (mixed quant profile q4_0 for embeddings-heavy routes, q8_0 for gen-heavy endpoints) with 48-concurrent stream slots per node looks like the right starting point for p99=~450–520ms in our lab runs for your request mix.
- Canary cadence you propose is fine operationally; two constraints to call out: (1) cold KV cache can add 20–60ms per request during ramp unless we pre-warm with a mirror pass; (2) sustained peak bursts >800rps will need brief burst capacity (we can reserve 1–2 spare nodes for 24–72h post-cutover).

Next steps I propose: 
1) 30-min call tomorrow to review the sizing workbook and lock in observability gates (latency, error rate, token cost delta). I can book 10:00–10:30 PT or 15:00–15:30 PT.
2) If we agree, we’ll push the prelim sizing into a dedicated staging pool for an internal smoke run (48h) and give you results.
3) Ben will author a concise cutover checklist for runbook ops; Marissa will align commercial cadence and commit dates.

I’ve added the drive link with a working doc: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/dedicated/onboard/ANT-2028-07-01-sizing

Attaching: prelim-sizing-estimate-antheum.xlsx

—Vivek
VP, Customer Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@antheum.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Antheum traffic profile + ask: sizing confirmation for Dedicated port

Elaine / team —

Thanks — read the sample and Vivek’s starter numbers look reasonable from a cost/perf tradeoff. A couple of commercial and operational notes to align before we lock a week: 

- Commitment window: to secure reserved capacity pricing we need an initial 3-month reserved term. We can scope burst capacity billing separately for the 72-hour post-cutover buffer.
- Acceptance gates: we will require a traffic-mirroring smoke run (48h) with the following pass criteria: no >1.5x increase in token cost per completion, p99 <= 550ms, and error rate <=0.3% for the mirrored load. Karthik, can you confirm acceptance test ownership and a rough calendar for the staging run?
- Cutover proposal: target window July 22–24 for the canary + ramp (subject to slot availability). We’ll aim for a 5% canary for 48h, then a 6-hour linear ramp to 100% with a one-hour holdback to verify telemetry.

If that works, legal will draft the SOW and we’ll sync on the final budget line. Please confirm internal stakeholders who should be CC’d on the SOW and whether Antheum needs an on-prem connector or VPC peering (that changes networking lead time).

On the pre-warm question: yes — we recommend a mirrored warmup pass for the top 500 prefixes to minimize cold-KV impact. We can run that in a scheduled 2-hour window before canary start.

Next: Vivek and I are available for the call tomorrow 10:00 PT. I’ll send an invite and include a short agenda.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@antheum.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-05T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Antheum traffic profile + ask: sizing confirmation for Dedicated port

Elaine / team — following up with an operational checklist and final ask list so we can convert the prelim sizing into an executed staging run. Draft cutover-checklist attached. Main items: 

- Staging pool build: 4 nodes as per Vivek’s workbook + 1 warm spare (tagged ANT-warm-01)
- Network: confirm VPC peering details or IP allowlist by July 12 to avoid infra delay
- Observability hooks: distributed traces + per-route token burn and KV-hit-rate collection (we’ll provide Grafana dashboards)
- Mirror run: schedule 48h mirror for July 18–19; pass gates per Marissa’s note. If pass, schedule canary July 22 start.
- Runbook ops: we will perform a pre-warm pass for top prefixes (2h), start 5% canary, execute 48h monitoring, then 6-hour linear ramp to 100% with rollback thresholds defined in the checklist.

Please acknowledge these actions and confirm contacts for the network/VPC owner at Antheum (ops@antheum.com is fine if monitored). Once I have network owner and legal SOW contact, I’ll finalize the cutover-checklist and send a formal runbook for sign-off.

Attachments: cutover-checklist-antheum.md
